description: The Unit of Environmental Engineering at the University of Innsbruck lists tools for generating virtual water infrastructure for benchmarking. DynaVIBe-Web is a free web front end that generates water distribution networks for any place on Earth from OpenStreetMap data, a digital elevation model, a drawn supply area, water sources and parameters such as total demand and a loop index, and returns sets of EPANET2 input files; it was used to build the semi-virtual virtRome case with 150,630 nodes and 157,044 pipes. The page also offers installers for a stochastic approach to generating urban drainage systems with 250 case study input files and maps, a stochastic approach for performance testing of water distribution systems, and a systematic generator of virtual supply networks, and lists the VIBe and DynaVIBe research projects. Coverage is any location with OpenStreetMap and elevation data. Access is free through the web application and downloads. Caveats: no licence is stated, the DynaVIBe-Web server did not respond from the cloud, and the VIBe and DynaVIBe project links now redirect to the unit's home page. Simulation uses: testing design, resilience and optimisation methods across many synthetic networks. Related records: the Kentucky water distribution database (data-uky-water-distribution-system-research-database), EPANET (model-epanet) and CityDrain3 (model-citydrain3-integrated-urban-drainage-toolbox).
